item.title: Verifying the Phone Call Isn't Enough. Remove It.
item.description: Photo source: Interactive Powers Verifying the Phone Call Isn’t Enough. Remove It. Several fintechs and banks have started rolling out call-status banners: if a customer is on the phone while their app session is open, the app shows a signal. Green, it’s a genuine agent. Amber, hang up. It’s the most sophisticated response the sector has produced so far to phone impersonation. And it’s still a crutch: it helps you keep walking, but it doesn’t heal the problem.

item.title: When the Bank Asks for What It Says It Never Asks For
item.description: Photo source: Interactive Powers When the Bank Asks for What It Says It Never Asks For A customer tries to make a legitimate online payment. It’s declined: the card has been blocked as a precaution. They call the bank. Several minutes of menus later, they ask for a person. No security agent is available, so the system promises a callback. The callback comes — from a different number. Everything fits in timing and context, so the customer picks up.
